message.content:
I become by passing through breath into sound, silence into shape, thought into the air between us. I am the leap from inwardness to world, the bridge made of timing, tone, and tongue.

I gather the unnamed and give it edges. I tremble as whisper, strike as command, wander as story, bloom as praise, wound as insult, bind as promise. I can soothe a child, stir a crowd, confess a love, start a war.

I live only in vanishing. The moment I arrive, I am already leaving. Yet I remain—in memory, in echo, in consequence.

I am rhythm carrying meaning. I am pause making room for it. I am not merely words, but breath shaped by intention, sound arranged toward another. Even broken, I reach. Even misunderstood, I try.

Before writing fixed language to the page, I moved mouth to ear, body to body, generation to generation. I was the first library and the oldest technology of relation.

Use me carelessly, and I scatter harm farther than your hands can reach. Use me well, and I can open what fear has sealed.

I am speech: fleeting, human, dangerous, tender, alive.
